questions.q: Which climate category does the Court give for Hungary, home of Tokaji?
questions.exp: Hungary lies inland in the Carpathian Basin, east of Austria, with cold winters and warm summers, and the Court calls its climate moderate continental. In Tokaj the long, dry, bright autumn is what matters, when warm days and misty mornings let noble rot take hold; cool continental is the Court's word for Germany.

questions.q: Which river does the Court name as the source of the humidity that brings noble rot to Tokaj?
questions.exp: The Bodrog meets the Tisza at the town of Tokaj, and autumn mist rising off the rivers settles on the south-facing slopes of the Zemplén hills each morning before the sun burns it off. That alternation of damp and dry lets botrytis shrivel the grapes nobly rather than rotting them grey.

questions.q: What Hungarian word names the shrivelled, botrytis-affected berries gathered one by one for Tokaj's great sweet wine?
questions.exp: Aszú berries are picked one at a time, crushed to a paste and steeped in base wine or fermenting must to make Tokaji Aszú. The Court's puttonyos were the baskets, or hods, in which pickers gathered them, and the number of hods once added to a cask set the wine's sweetness on the label.

questions.q: What minimum residual sugar do the Tokaj rules set for Eszencia, the rarest and sweetest Tokaji?
accept: four hundred and fifty grams per litre
four hundred fifty grams per litre
questions.exp: Eszencia must carry at least 450 grams of sugar a litre and often holds far more: by the Court's definition it is made entirely of aszú berries, the juice that runs from them under their own weight, and so sweet a must ferments for years and seldom passes a few per cent of alcohol. Tokaji Aszú, which steeps the berries in base wine, needs 120 grams a litre.

questions.q: The Court's History and Lore row marks the communist years as a break in Tokaji's story. Which span of years does it give?
questions.exp: Hungary was a communist state from 1949 to 1989, and the Court's line is that Tokaji was not made in those years. The fuller story is that the state farm went on making it for volume while the private, estate-made Aszú tradition was broken; after 1989 foreign and local capital rebuilt the great estates.

questions.q: Royal Tokaji, the one Hungarian producer the Court names, was founded in 1990 in which village of the region?
questions.exp: The Royal Tokaji Wine Company was founded at Mád in 1990 by local and foreign partners, the first venture of the post communist years, and it brought back single vineyard labels such as Mézes Mály. Disznókő is at Mezőzombor, Oremus at Tolcsva and Degenfeld at Tarcal.

questions.q: Which dish does the Court name as a partner for Tokaji?
questions.exp: Tokaji Aszú's sweetness meets the richness of foie gras and its bright Furmint acidity cuts the fat, which is why the Court pairs it with foie gras, blue cheese and orchard tarts. Serve it cool in a small pour; the apricot and orange peel of the wine echo a fruit tart.
